anomalies.observed: A green wire runs from the VCC net (labelled VCC near the top-right of the board) to the XTAL1/PB3 pin of U2 (ATtiny45-20P, pin 2). That pin carries the POT label, which is the net for the potentiometer wiper on J3 pin 2. The POT net is therefore tied directly to the VCC supply.
anomalies.expected: The POT net should only connect the potentiometer wiper (J3.2) to the ATtiny45 PB3 analog input, with no direct connection to the 5 V supply. The wiper should be driven by the divider, not by the rail.

evidence.quote: Sheet: / (single page): green wire from label VCC to U2 XTAL1/PB3 pin 2, where the POT label is attached to the same pin; J3 pin 2 labelled POT
The specification describes the intended design: its purpose, architecture, key components and their values, power rails and interfaces.

anomalies.impact: The potentiometer sense line is held at the supply voltage, so the POT reading is wrong or fixed. The wiper can also be forced to the rail, which can damage the pot or the MCU pin and stop the speed control from working.

parsed.summary: The schematic shows a wire tying the VCC supply to the POT net at the ATtiny45 XTAL1/PB3 pin, which would short the potentiometer sense line to the supply. The spec gives no sourcing that would explain this, so it is most likely a wiring error or tampering.
